2. `session` (better-auth) — id, userId→user(CASCADE), token?, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt
3. `account` (better-auth) — id, userId→user(CASCADE), accountId, providerId, **accessToken, refreshToken** (plaintext), expiresAt, password, createdAt, updatedAt
4. `verification` (better-auth) — id, identifier, value, expiresAt, createdAt
5. `workflow` — id(wf_), userId→user, objective, status (9 states), schemaVersion, archivedAt, createdAt, updatedAt
6. `workflow_execution` — id(exe_), workflowId→workflow, status (8 states), reason, prompt, costUsd, tokenCount
7. `workflow_step` — id(step_), workflowId→workflow, executionId, kind, assistantText, status, order, idempotencyKey
8. `tool_execution` — id(tool_), workflowId, executionId (set null), stepId (set null), order, tool, provider, status, input jsonb, output jsonb, errorCode, durationMs
9. `agent_state` — id(agent_state_), workflowId, phase, status, version (optimistic), data jsonb
10. `approval` — id(ap_), workflowId, executionId (CASCADE), userId, toolName, input, status (pending), reason, decidedAt
11. `event` — id(evt_), workflowId (CASCADE), executionId (set null), type, data jsonb, occurredAt
12. `notification` — id(ntf_), userId, workflowId (set null), type, channel, subject, body, deliveredAt, readAt
13. `observation` — id(obs_), workflowId, type, content jsonb, observedAt
14. `recovery_attempt` — id(rec_), workflowId, executionId, failureClass, failureCode, attempt, strategy, result, detail, completedAt
15. `schedule` — id(sched_), workflowId, cron, intervalSeconds, nextRunAt, lastRunAt, enabled, config
16. `webhook_board` — id(whk_), tokenHash (unique), instruction, status, expiresAt, usedAt

> Better-auth `account.access_token`/`refresh_token` + `password` live in
> plaintext columns — snapshot then DROP with the auth tables.

**Command**: `bun db:generate` (turbo `-F @aevryn/db`) with migrations out dir.
Commit this as `001_old_schema_snapshot.sql` in a `migrations/` folder.

## Step 2 — Unexpected-but-simple wins (kill in snapshot while migrating)
- Delete better-auth 4 tables (auth moves to Supabase Auth).
- Delete `webhook_board` (replaced by in-app webhooks via Supabase Realtime +
  RPC; MVP doesn't need external token hooks).
- Delete `agent_state`, `recovery_attempt`, `event`, `observation` (the new
  schema folds activity into different tables; see SCHEMA.md).

## Step 3 — Supabase-init
- `supabase init` already done (`config.toml`). Set `schema_paths`, add
  `seed.sql` (insert PERSONAL workspace for new users via a trigger instead —
  prefer DB trigger → no seed file needed).
- Auth providers: enable Google (`[auth.external.google] enabled = true`,
  create provider in Supabase dashboard with Google OAuth app).
- Realtime: enable `wal_level=logical` for Postgres → Realtime broadcasts.

## Step 4 — Orders of tables (all `create index ... if not exists`)
See SCHEMA.md for full DDL roadmap. Create order:
1. identity/auth users (`auth.users` exists) → 2. workspaces → 3. profiles →
4. threads (per workspace) → 5. workflows (bound to threads) →
6. chat_messages → 7. runs / runs_activity → 8. plans + plan_steps →
9. memories (thread-scoped, mem0-backed idempotent mirror) →
10. notifications → 11. approval_requests → 12. api_keys → 13. files.

## Guardrails
- Run `supabase db advisors` after migration; fix issues before proceeding
  (supabase skill requirement).
- RLS on EVERY table (`TO authenticated` + owner predicate `using/auth.uid()`).
- Keep `drizzle-kit` as tool, but treat Supabase as source of truth; generate
  drizzle migration only when required for type-check parity.

input.newString:
- **RLS policy list**:
  - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
    files (+ own invites).
  - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
    chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
    OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
  - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
    `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
    group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
  - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
    `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
    workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
    exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
    → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
- **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
  `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
  `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + default `groups`
  (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS) automatically.

## Why this shape (reasoning)
- `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
  sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
- `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
  group; INVITES is virtual, derived from `thread_shares`). Group/thread
  limits (≤5 threads/group, ≤3 groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.

# ARCHITECTURE — Full New Backend + Frontend Logic

Replaces the old tRPC + regex-decision + god-class backend. The system becomes:

```
Browser (Next.js client, zustand stores)
   │  useChat (Vercel AI SDK @ai-sdk/react 4.x)
   ▼
/workspace/[threadId]   (client page, no full reload on threadId swap)
   │
   ▼  POST /api/chat (ChatTransport → streamText)
   │
   ├── live (fast) tools: askUserQuestion, showPlan, editPlan, memory tools,
   │                      HTTP request tool, media tools (image/transcription live)
   │
   └── durable (Anakin/Inngest) tools: delegateAgenticWork (one tool)
               │
               ▼  inngest.send("thread/run")
               ▼  Inngest fn "thread-runner" streams run_activities rows
               ▼  Supabase Realtime → ChatMessage updates live in place
```

## A. Auth (Supabase, Google only, MVP)

- Root `page.tsx` = login screen. `supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider:"google"})`.
- `onLinkIdentity`/redirect to `/workspace` after signup.
- Post-signup flow: pre-questions driven by a JSON config (role/usecase/goal,
  multi+single select; user edits the JSON, app maps it to QuestionFlow). Answers
  → `user_profiles.pre_answers`. If signup exists but profile row missing → auto
  navigate to onboarding (create on demand).
- `useSupabaseUser()` hook (zustand + Supabase client). Middleware/proxy
  (`src/proxy.ts` evlog) still runs; tRPC session shim removed — server routes
  read `createServerClient` session from cookies.
- Sessions: Supabase handles refresh (`@supabase/ssr` cookie-based). Server
  side: `createServerClient` with anon/publishable; protected route checks user.

## F. Frontend state (zustand)

- Zustand stores (each `[thread]`, `[sidebar]`, `[chatComposer]`, `[ui/theme]`,
  `[auth]`) — keeps server components pure; zustand used max; no useState sprawl.
- `threadId` navigation: Next.js `router.push('/workspace/'+id, { scroll:false })`
  updating only param; page reads `params.threadId` once → store. ChatComposer
  layout: centered when no messages → bottom once first message exists.
- ChatComposer: queue (ordered, editable, removable, durable-backend),
  token-quality slider formula: `maxTokens per CHAT request` (this is what the
  slider means; maps to `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, not a run budget),
  file/image/pdf attach → compress (canvas, WebP, quality 0.8, max 2000px) →
  Supabase Storage → `files` row + `UIMessage` attachments.
- Queue `chat_messages.status=queued`: on run finish, drain SEQUENTIALLY —
  deliver message, wait for that response to finish, then next (no parallel
  queue burst). Edited/reordered queue → DB rows updated in place, order kept.

## G. Memory (mem0, ONE place per user, thread-scoped)

- ONE mem0 store per app user (as chosen): every thread's memories live there,
  scoped by `metadata.threadId`. `storeMemory`/`searchMemory` tools:
  - thread scope: `{scope:"thread", threadId}` — memories only reprompted for
    that thread.
  - global scope: `{scope:"global"}` — **program-given memory injected
    beforehand**, works across ALL workspaces/threads/apps for that user (not
    per-workspace). E.g. capability schemas, user prefs, standing instructions.
- `packages/agent/src/adapters/README.md:1` resolution: adapter schemas exposed
  to LLM via GLOBAL memory (per decision) — one tool `listCapabilities` returns
  schemas; keeps them OO-reflectable.

input.newString:
## I. Permission model — invites, roles, sharing (locked answers)

### Role set (ONE model everywhere)
`owner | editor | viewer` — **no admin**. | Action | owner | editor | viewer | thread-guest |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| rename / delete workspace, keys, settings | ✅ | — | — | — |
| manage members (invite/role/remove) | ✅ | — | — | — |
| create / rename / delete groups & threads | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| edit plans, bind workflows | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| send msgs, run/stop, approve approvals | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ |
| view history / runs / plan | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| rename / rebind / re-share / delete shared thread | ✅ | — | — | — |
> thread-guest = the person invited to a SPECIFIC thread (thread share). Editor
> = member of the shared workspace.

### Workspace invite (join the REAL workspace)
1. Owner (only) copies workspace invite link / shares by email → `invites` row
   (`kind=workspace`, role editor|viewer chosen at invite).
2. Invitee accepts → `workspace_members` row (role as invited). NO copy, no new
   workspace — it's the owner's actual workspace. Workspace appears in the
   invitee's top-left switcher (badge on the button) → switching in shows ALL
   groups + threads (all members see everything).
3. Members chat/run using the **workspace's keys** (owner pays) UNLESS profile
   toggle "use my own keys in invited workspaces" is on → member's own
   workspace keys are used. `get_workspace_key` RPC + key-service honor this.
4. Owner can change roles / remove / revoke anytime. Editor can delete any
   thread/group (even others'). Viewer read-only.

### Thread share (guest in YOUR sidebar)
1. Owner toggles `threads.share_enabled` and copies the thread share link
   (per-thread; the "list of my threads + switch" UI in Members/Share).
2. Invitee accepts → `thread_shares` row. The LIVE SAME thread (not a copy)
   appears in the invitee's OWN workspace sidebar under the **virtual INVITES
   group**, with a Badge on the thread button and on the header. Both users
   chat in the same realtime thread.
3. Invitee's messages use **their own keys**; their name shows on user bubbles.
4. Owner revokes by flipping share_enabled / deleting the share.

### Keys resolution order (chat / run)
```
1. member in a shared workspace + prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
      → member's OWN Personal workspace keys (type: groq|anakin|mem0|…)
2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
3. env defaults (ANAKIN_API_KEY / GROQ_API_KEY / MEM0_API_KEY / models)
```

+4. Owner can change roles / remove / revoke anytime. Editor can delete any

parts.text: Now PLAN.md:

input.newString:
## P0 — Groundwork & migrations (prereq for everything)
- [ ] Supabase local running; `supabase init` config sanity (`config.toml`
      `schema_paths`, real migrate workflow). Create `001_old_schema_snapshot`
      via drizzle-kit (see `db/MIGRATION.md`).
- [ ] `supabase/migrations` seed enforcement (drop seed file, use trigger).
- [ ] `scripts/` service helpers updated (no destructive ops in CI).
- [ ] Verify `bun run db:generate` produces snapshot; commit as baseline.
- **Verify**: `supabase migration list --local` shows snapshot applied.

## P1 — Auth (Supabase, Google-only) + onboarding
- [ ] Env: add `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, service role server.
- [ ] `packages/auth`: rewrite to Supabase server/client init (replace
      better-auth). `src/lib/supabase-server.ts` + `supabase-client.ts`.
- [ ] Middleware/proxy `src/proxy.ts` auth-aware (session guard).
- [ ] `on_auth_user_created` trigger (SQL): Personal workspace + profile +
      owner membership + default groups (PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS).
- [ ] Root `page.tsx`: login (Google); post-signup onboarding questions flow
      driven by a JSON config (multi+single) → persist in `pre_answers`.
      Auto-navigate to onboarding if profile row is missing.
- **Verify**: Google login → Personal workspace exists → onboarding → workspace.

## P2 — New DB schema (see db/SCHEMA.md)
- [ ] `supabase migration new new_schema` → all 17 tables + enums + RLS +
      indexes + storage bucket `chat-attachments` + Realtime enabled for
      4 tables (chat_messages, run_activities, approval_requests,
      notifications). Tables incl. NEW: `groups`, `invites`, `thread_shares`;
      `workspace_members.role` = owner|editor|viewer (no admin).
- [ ] Group/thread limits enforced (≤5 threads/group, ≤3 groups/workspace
      free) via insert RPC/trigger.
- [ ] Drizzle types parity: regenerate `packages/db/src/schema` from new SQL.
- [ ] Drop legacy tables (auth/session/account/verification, webhook_board,
      agent_state, recovery_attempt, event, observation) in migration.
- [ ] `supabase db advisors` clean.
- **Verify**: advisors pass; RLS smoke test (anon/authenticated) via psql.

## P3 — Services (packages/workflow split; drop tRPC god router)
- [ ] `thread-service` (threads CRUD, search, title rename, bind, group move).
- [ ] `plan-service` (plans + plan_steps CRUD, accept/decline).
- [ ] `run-service` (runs lifecycle end-to-end + sequential queue drain).
- [ ] `activity-service` (run_activities insert/stream, sub-task nest).
- [ ] `notification-service` + `approval-service` + `key-service` (Vault +
      resolution: member-override → workspace → env).
- [ ] `member-service` (invites: workspace+thread, accept/fan-out, roles,
      revoke priorities re thread_shares).
- [ ] `memory-service` (mem0 ONE store per user, thread-metadata scoping,
      global = program-given).
- [ ] Remove `@aevryn/api` tRPC agent router usage (routes now REST/chat).
      Keep `GET /api/health` if wanted.
- **Verify**: services unit-tested against local Supabase (vitest).

## P4 — Inngest (rebuild functions directory)
- [ ] `thread/run` event + `thread-runner` (streaming run_activities, cost cap
      BEFORE steps, idempotent gate via `runs.status`).
- [ ] `schedule-tick` FIXED: real Inngest cron trigger + registered with all
      functions in `/api/inngest` serve.
- [ ] `notification-notifier` registered (webhook/in-app).
- [ ] Remove execution-run legacy + regex decision parsing; prompts centralized
      (`packages/agent/src/prompts.ts` per PROMPTS.md).
- **Verify**: `bun inngest:dev` + `bun dev` — run a sample delegation;
      `run_activities` rows appear; realtime arrives in UI.

## P5 — Chat route + live tools (the heart)
- [ ] `POST /api/chat` route: `streamText` + `ChatTransport`,
      `toUIMessageStream`, `createUIMessageStreamResponse`; session-aware;
      honor member key override before resolving workspace/env keys.
- [ ] Tools: `askQuestion`, `showPlan` (NO auto-plan — only on explicit
      user request), `editPlan`, `bindWorkflow`/`finalizeAndInject`,
      `storeMemory`, `searchMemory`, `httpRequest` (safe defaults),
      `delegateAgenticWork` (durable bridge), `listCapabilities`,
      `generateImage`/`transcribeAudio` (lazy per configured model).
- [ ] Tool schemas = zod; `AskUserQuestion` schema shared server/client.
- [ ] Auto-approve switch honored + system "auto-approved" msg.
- [ ] Attachments: image/pdf → LLM-readable parts (image data-URL, pdf text).
- [ ] Token `quality` slider = max tokens per chat request → `maxOutputTokens`.
- **Verify**: scenarios 1–3 from ARCHITECTURE §K pass end-to-end.

## P6 — Durable queue + attachments
- [ ] `POST /api/queue` drain SEQUENTIALLY (deliver → wait finish → next);
      queued rows durable; ChatComposer reads DB queue; edit/reorder persists
      order + content.
- [ ] Image compression (canvas→WebP quality 0.8, ≤2000px) → storage → `files`.
- [ ] ChatMessage attachment props extended (`images/video/audio/pdf`).
- **Verify**: close tab mid-queue + reopen → queue intact + delivers in order.

## P7 — Frontend wiring (zustand + realtime + widgets)
- [ ] Stores: useAuthStore, useThreadStore, useComposerStore, useSidebarStore,
      useNotificationsStore, useUIStore.
- [ ] `useRealtimeThread(threadId)` subscription → merges broadcast rows.
- [ ] workspace/[threadId] page: real chat load, router push w/o reload,
      composer center→bottom, header real rename + workflow dropdown.
- [ ] AppSidebar: real NAV_SECTIONS (groups from DB incl. virtual INVITES),
      search, notifications chip + mark-read, run-all/stop-all PARALLEL
      (groups ≤5), per-item run/stop/rename/share/delete.
- [ ] WorkflowDialog: rename Instructions→Agent + Environment tab + General/
      Share/Plan/Memories wired to real data; delete-confirm works.
- [ ] Settings/Profile dialogs: Workspace group (General + Members) vs Global
      group (Notifications/Appearance/Security). Members: InputCopy link +
      list w/ role Select (owner/editor/viewer) + Remove. Profile: "use my own
      keys in invited workspaces" toggle.
- [ ] Invite UI: workspace link invite; thread share toggle list; Badge on
      thread button (INVITES group) + thread header; workspace switcher badge.
- **Verify**: page-manual QA checklist (scenarios 4–8 in ARCHITECTURE §K).

## P8 — Sub-agents container + markdown (FUTURE phases, stubs designed)
- [ ] `run_activities.parent_id` sub-agent container merge (parallel).
- [ ] Markdown/table renderer (existing Table component; output contract ready).
- **Verify**: sub-agent demo.

## Definition of done (MVP)
- Google-only auth; JSON-driven onboarding; workspace membership (invites,
  owner/editor/viewer, all-threads-visible, key override toggle); thread
  sharing (INVITES group + badge, guest chat/run, own keys, owner revoke).
- Workspaces (Personal + joined) + threads + bound workflows via LLM tools only
  (NO auto-plan).
- Live chat streaming + durable Anakin runs streaming to ThinkingSteps.
- Queue durability (sequential) + auto-approve + notifications chip +
  per-workspace keys + media (image/transcription).
- No hardcoded mock data; all mocked UI wired to DB; tRPC removed.

input.newString:
## Where the USER enters their own keys (UI)

Primary → **Workflow Settings dialog → "Agent" tab** (rename of
"Instructions"), with an **"Environment"** subsection:

- Groq API key + Groq model (text)
- Anakin API key + base URL
- Mem0 API key
- (secondary) Image / Speech / Transcription / Video model overrides

Stored in DB table `workspace_api_keys`:
`workspace_id | user_id | provider | key_name | key_value(encrypted) | created_at`.

Resolution order at call time:
```
1. member of a SHARED workspace + user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
     → member's OWN Personal workspace keys
2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
3. env default
```
`workflow_api_keys` optional per-thread override keyed same way (rare).
Encryption: AES-256-GCM with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env (add to server env) — or
Supabase Vault (`vault.create_secret`) if service_role available. Recommend
**Supabase Vault** — no extra env key, native audit.

> Note: ChatComposer token slider = "max tokens per chat request" — maps to
> `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, NOT a run budget. Server caps
> (`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` etc.) remain hard ceilings.

parts.text: Now NOTES.md — append the decisions (answers) section + update role enum:

input.newString:
## User's new rules
- Auth: Google Supabase ONLY for MVP. Pre-signup questions (who are you: student/
  engineer/AI engineer/...) → profile. Root page.tsx = login screen.
- Workspace "PERSONAL" auto-created per user. MVP single workspace. Schema scalable.
- Sidebar: section search by thread title, notifications chip + mark-read-on-open,
  New btn → new workflow GROUP, group dropdown run all/stop all/rename/delete all,
  workflow item name + status icon + hover run/stop/rename/3-dot.
- Header: dropdown (workflows) + inline rename input. Run/Stop btn only if
  workflow BOUND by toolcall. Workflow settings btn.
- Chat: useChat direct; LLM tools (zod+schema+desc); Anakin tool calls → Inngest
  durable; Inngest returns schematic JSON → ThinkingSteps realtime (sub-tasks too,
  e.g. "reading portfolio/about.html/projects.html"). SystemMessage on error/
  warning/retry; new ChatMessage(assistant) only when error/warning/workflow
  stops/restarts — append same message when running. QuestionFlow parent for
  questionflow, workflowbindingapproval, event approval. Plan editable anyplace.
  LLM decides plan yes/no/steps; user approval UI = workflowApproval questions
  (approve/decline/bind-not-run/request-changes). Decline destroys plan.
  Auto-approve switch → auto Approve + system msg "auto approved via settings".
- Queued messages durable (close window safe). ChatComposer center → bottom after
  first msg; route swap `workspace/<threadId>` no reload. Media: image/pdf upload,
  compress image w/o quality loss → supabase storage. Markdown later (table comp
  ready). Mediums: text, image, speech, transcription, video (per model settings).
- sub-agents parallel later (container collects). mem0 per-thread + global tool.
  zustand for client state; keep server components.
- DB: migrate OLD schema → migration file (snapshot) FIRST, then write NEW schema
  w/ FKs + best practices. No docstrings in code. No hardcoding.
- Deliverables: questions.md, features.md, UI file, PROMPTS file (all prompts in
  one place, export/import), final-docs organizing everything. Env analysis.

## Decisions (locked answers, 2026 round 2)
- Roles ONE set everywhere: **owner | editor | viewer** (admin DROPPED).
  Workspace: owner full (settings/keys/members), editor works (create/edit/run/
  delete ANY thread+group, edit plans), viewer read-only. Thread: owner =
  threads.user_id; guests via thread_shares role editor|viewer.
- **Workspace invite** = join the owner's REAL workspace (no copy): accept →
  workspace_members row; all threads visible to all members; member mgmt owner
  only; editor can delete ANY thread; viewers read-only.
- **Keys in shared workspace**: workspace keys (owner pays) by default;
  profile toggle `prefer_own_keys_in_shared` → member's OWN Personal keys.
  Resolution: member-override → workspace → env.
- **Thread share** = live SAME thread (not fork): guest sees it in their own
  sidebar under virtual INVITES group + Badge (thread button right, beside
  count number; also on header). Guest uses OWN keys; sends msgs with their
  name; CANNOT rename/edit plan/bind/re-share/delete. Owner revoke instant.
  Owner toggles per-thread `threads.share_enabled` (switch list UI).
- Onboarding questions: JSON config (user edits), multi+single select, stored
  pre_answers jsonb; auto-navigate to onboarding if profile missing.
- NO auto-plan: LLM never showPlan/bind alone; only on explicit user ask.
  2nd msg ≠ plan. Bind → Run shows/Stop hidden; Run toggles→Stop while running.
- Token `quality` slider = max tokens PER CHAT request (maxOutputTokens), NOT
  run budget.
- ≤5 threads per group, ≤3 groups per workspace (free) — enforced at insert;
  group run-all/stop-all runs PARALLEL.
- Queue: durable DB rows; drain SEQUENTIAL (deliver → wait finish → next);
  editable/reordered rows persist order+content.
- Media: image + transcription SHIPPED (lazy if IMAGE_MODEL/TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL

Also FEATURES.md has "workspace = personal + joined" — fine. Also MIGRATION step 3 mention INVITES already in step 4. Also FEATURES #12 mentions "INVITES group (Badge on thread + header)" - fine.

Now the product brainstorm question. The user asks: "is there any other simplification or features that you want to add so that the tool becomes very good or an actual product?"

Let me give a crisp list of high-value simplifications + features, then ask which to adopt via question tool. This is a creative/advisory ask — appropriate to give a good list. Keep tight.

Done — INVITES now a real locked system group. 

Now the product question. Here's my shortlist of **simplifications** (cut friction) + **features** (make it a product). Fraud-filtered to what matches your architecture already:

**Simplifications (do these, low cost, high payoff)**
1. **Draft thread trash** — one workflow-delete "soft archive" (recoverable 30 days) instead of instant hard-delete. Cheap, saves users lives. (Or keep hard-delete; your call.)
2. **Smart default title** — auto-title thread from first message ("Laptop comparison") instead of blank "New thread". Users never rename.
3. **One "Run" mental model** — Run button + LLM both trigger `thread/run`; workflowApproval dialog has 4 buttons max (Approve+Run / Approve / Decline / Edit plan). No dead dropdowns.
4. **Model presets per provider** — Agent/Env tab loads a *hardcoded known-good model list* per provider with search, PLUS free-text override for power users. Kills the "what do I type?" moment (your Groq model confusion).
5. **Empty-state onboarding kick** — on very first workspace visit, a 3-line guided example thread ("try 'plan me a laptop comparison'") user can run instantly. Proves the product in 60s.

**Features (actual product)**
6. **Thread sharing via link without login-guess** — share link preview page shows thread title + owner name before accepting (no leak of content pre-accept).
7. **Activity journal per run** — timeline of `run_activities` (steps, costs, tokens, retries) in a collapsible "log" drawer. Introspection → trust → power.
8. **Export/import thread** — single JSON (plan + steps + key messages; keys stripped) share/file. Great for templates, "marketplace later".
9. **Scheduled/instant "re-run"** — rerun last run with same plan (no new chat). Pairs with your schedule-tick cron.
10. **Usage dashboard (pricing enabler)** — runs.cost_usd + token_count already recorded → simple monthly usage + quota meter (5 threads/group, 3 groups). Monetization hook.
11. **Template gallery** — preseed 5 templates ("Research competitor", "Scrape + summarize", etc.) as read-only threads you duplicate → your own onboarding/retention loop.

input.newString:
## L. Non-goals / pinned decisions
- Markdown rendering: FUTURE (write API to be parser-friendly — parts, no
  prose-heavy gating). Output contract ready for it.
- Media generation: IMAGE + TRANSCRIPTION SHIPPED in MVP (lazy-load provider
  when `IMAGE_MODEL`/`TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` configured); SPEECH/VIDEO stay schemas
  only until models exist. Attachments always converted to LLM-readable parts.
- Sub-agents in parallel: FUTURE phase (see FEATURES.md); design tool outputs as
  containers so sub-agent results merge into `run_activities`.
- Creating MULTIPLE owned workspaces: FUTURE (pro tier). MVP = 1 owned
  Personal + unlimited JOINED workspaces (via invite).
- Shared-thread plan editing by guests: OFF (owner/editor only).

## Product features (locked in docs; see NOTES "Decisions" & PLAN.md)
1. **Soft-archive delete**: deleting a thread/workflow sets `threads.deleted_at`;
   recoverable 30 days (trash), then hard-delete incl. Storage. Never silent.
2. **Smart auto-title**: thread title automatically set from the first user
   message (truncated); rename still available. No blank "New thread".
3. **One Run mental model**: Run button AND the LLM both fire `thread/run`
   (same event). WorkflowApproval dialog = max 4 buttons: Approve+Run /
   Approve / Decline / Edit plan. No dead dropdowns.
4. **Model presets**: Agent/Env tab shows a per-provider list of known model
   ids (searchable) + free-text override; picks write `workspace_api_keys.model_name`.
5. **Share preview page**: share link lands on a preview (thread title + owner
   name only, NO content) with Accept — content stays private until accepted.
6. **Export/import thread**: single JSON (plan + steps + key messages,
   keys stripped) for export/import — template/reuse path.
7. **Re-run**: from a past Run play a rerun with the same plan, no new chat
   (`runs.rerun_of`, trigger=rerun).

-# Aevryn - Project Instructions
-
-## 0. INSTRUCTIONS
-
-1. TypeScript uses camelCase.
-2. PostgreSQL uses snake_case.
-3. JSON/API responses use camelCase.
-4. HTTP routes use /api/v1/<resource>.
-5. All externally visible IDs use prefixed ULIDs.
-6. All timestamps are UTC and use timestamptz in PostgreSQL.
-7. All persisted schemas have a schemaVersion when evolution is expected.
-8. Validate external input with Zod.
-9. Never parse LLM free-form text to control runtime behavior.
-10. Never let the LLM directly mutate the database.
-11. All agent decisions must pass schema validation.
-12. All external side effects must be durable/idempotent.
-13. Never store secrets in state, memory, tool input/output, or logs.
-14. Never log credentials, cookies, tokens, or full prompts by default.
-15. Separate workflow, execution, step, state, observation, memory, and event concepts.
-16. Do not put all history into one JSONB field.
-17. Use composition rather than deep inheritance.
-18. Keep provider-specific logic inside provider adapters.
-19. Forge core must not depend directly on Anakin implementation details.
-20. Do not introduce infrastructure unless there is a demonstrated requirement.
-21. Every new database table requires indexes based on actual query patterns.
-22. Every asynchronous external job must have an explicit lifecycle.
-23. Every retry must have a bounded retry/recovery budget.
-24. Consequential actions require an approval boundary when appropriate.
-25. Do not expose chain-of-thought; store concise reasoning summaries only.
-
-## 1. Project Identity
-
-Aevryn is a durable, self-healing web-agent platform.
-
-A user gives Aevryn a natural-language objective.
-
-Aevryn should be able to:
-
-1. Understand the objective.
-2. Plan how to accomplish it.
-3. Select appropriate capabilities.
-4. Execute those capabilities against the web.
-5. Observe external results.
-6. Persist workflow state.
-7. Decide what to do next.
-8. Recover from failures.
-9. Remember useful knowledge.
-10. Sleep when waiting is appropriate.
-11. Wake and resume later.
-12. Continue until the objective is completed, cancelled, or safely failed.
-
-Aevryn is NOT primarily a chatbot.
-
-The core product is a persistent objective-execution engine.
-
----
-
-# 2. Current Technology Stack
-
-## Application
-
-* TypeScript
-* Bun
-* Turborepo
-* Next.js
-* React
-* Tailwind CSS
-* shadcn/ui
-* tRPC
-* Better Auth
-* zustand (global client state)
-
-## Agent
-
-* Vercel AI SDK
-
-## Durable execution
-
-* Inngest
-
-## Database
-
-* Supabase PostgreSQL
-* Drizzle ORM
-* pgvector
-
-## Web capabilities
-
-* Anakin
-
-## Browser recovery
-
-* Stagehand
-
-## Validation
-
-* Zod
-
-## Testing
-
-* Vitest
-
-## Tooling
-
-* Biome
-* Lefthook
-* Evlog
-
-Do not introduce additional infrastructure without a concrete requirement.
-
-Do not add a dependency merely because it is popular.
-
----
-
-# 3. Architecture Principles
-
-Aevryn must remain modular and provider-independent.
-
-The fundamental architecture is:
-
-USER OBJECTIVE
-→ PLANNING
-→ CAPABILITY SELECTION
-→ WORKFLOW
-→ DURABLE EXECUTION
-→ WEB CAPABILITY
-→ OBSERVATION
-→ DECISION
-→ STATE / MEMORY
-→ CONTINUE / RECOVER / SLEEP / NOTIFY / FINISH
-
-The most important architectural rule is:
-
-> The LLM decides what should happen. Aevryn decides how it is safely and durably executed.
-
-The model must not directly control infrastructure or persistence.
-
----
-
-# 4. Responsibility Boundaries
-
-## Vercel AI SDK
-
-Responsible for:
-
-* LLM interaction
-* agent loops
-* tool calling
-* structured outputs
-* model context
-* tool definitions
-* AI reasoning interface
-* approval integration
-
-It is NOT the durable workflow engine.
-
-## Inngest
-
-Responsible for:
-
-* durable execution
-* retries
-* checkpoints
-* sleeping
-* waking
-* scheduled execution
-* event-triggered execution
-* failure handling
-
-Do not build a second workflow engine.
-
-## Anakin
-
-Responsible for external web capabilities.
-
-Potential capabilities include:
-
-* search
-* URL scraping
-* crawling/map
-* agentic search
-* Wire actions
-* browser operations
-
-Anakin-specific implementation details must remain behind an adapter.
-
-Aevryn core must not be tightly coupled to Anakin response formats.
-
-## Stagehand
-
-Stagehand is a browser reasoning/recovery capability.
-
-It is NOT the foundation of Aevryn.
-
-Use it when browser reasoning or structural recovery is necessary.
-
-## PostgreSQL
-
-PostgreSQL is the source of truth for structured persistent data.
-
-## pgvector
-
-pgvector provides semantic memory retrieval.
-
-Do not introduce a separate vector database.
-
-## Drizzle
-
-Drizzle is the typed database access/migration layer.
-
-Do not place business logic inside database schema definitions.
-
----
-
-# 5. Core Domain Concepts
-
-These concepts must remain separate.
-
-## Workflow
-
-A long-lived user objective.
-
-Example:
-
-"Monitor this product and tell me when its price falls below ₹5,000."
-
-## Execution
-
-One run of a workflow.
-
-A workflow may have many executions.
-
-## Step
-
-A durable unit of work inside an execution.
-
-## State
-
-The current internal state of a workflow.
-
-## Observation
-
-A representation of what Aevryn currently knows about the external world.
-
-## Result
-
-The direct output of an operation.
-
-## Tool Execution
-
-A record of a capability invocation.
-
-## Recovery Attempt
-
-A record of an attempt to recover from a failure.
-
-## Memory
-
-Knowledge worth preserving for future use.
-
-## Event
-
-An immutable record that something happened.
-
-Never use one generic object to represent all of these.
-
----
-
-# 6. State Rules
-
-Dynamic workflow state may use JSON/JSONB.
-
-However, frequently queried values should have normal database columns.
-
-Examples:
-
-* status
-* workflow_id
-* execution_id
-* user_id
-* timestamps
-* version
-* ownership
-
-Do not store the entire history of a workflow in one JSONB field.
-
-Current state is not historical event data.
-
-Current state is not memory.
-
-Current state is not observation history.
-
-The LLM must never directly mutate database state.
-
-The model may produce a state patch.
-
-The runtime validates the patch and applies it.
-
----
-
-# 7. LLM Control Rules
-
-Never parse arbitrary natural-language model responses to determine runtime behavior.
-
-Use structured schemas.
-
-Every runtime decision must be validated.
-
-Use Zod for:
-
-* user input
-* tool input
-* tool output where necessary
-* agent decisions
-* state patches
-* memory candidates
-* external API boundaries
-
-The model may propose:
-
-* tool calls
-* state patches
-* memories
-* next actions
-* recovery
-* sleep
-* notification
-* completion
-
-The runtime remains authoritative.
-
-Do not store chain-of-thought.
-
-Only store concise reasoning summaries when useful for observability.
-
----
-
-# 8. Capability Architecture
-
-Capabilities must be provider-independent.
-
-Prefer an interface similar to:
-
-interface Capability {
-name: string;
-description: string;
-inputSchema: ZodType;
-execute(input: unknown): Promise<CapabilityResult>;
-}
-
-Capabilities should be registered through a capability registry.
-
-The agent should discover capabilities through their descriptions and schemas.
-
-Provider-specific implementations belong in adapters.
-
-Example:
-
-searchWeb
-→ SearchCapability
-→ AnakinSearchAdapter
-
-The core agent should not need to know how Anakin implements search.
-
-Prefer composition over inheritance.
-
-Avoid deep class hierarchies.
-
----
-
-# 9. Failure Classification
-
-Every significant external failure should be classified.
-
-At minimum:
-
-### Transient
-
-Examples:
-
-* timeout
-* temporary provider outage
-* temporary rate limit
-
-Usually handled through durable retries.
-
-### Structural
-
-Examples:
-
-* page structure changed
-* target element disappeared
-* previous extraction strategy became invalid
-* browser target changed
-
-Handled by Aevryn recovery.
-
-### Fatal
-
-Examples:
-
-* invalid configuration
-* permanently unavailable authorization
-* invalid objective
-
-Safely fail.
-
-Never blindly retry every error.
-
-Never interpret a human-readable error message as the error's machine type.
-
-Use stable error codes.
-
----
-
-# 10. Recovery
-
-Recovery is a first-class system.
-
-Preferred flow:
-
-failure
-→ classify
-→ inspect
-→ retrieve relevant memory
-→ choose recovery strategy
-→ execute
-→ validate
-→ persist successful strategy
-→ continue
-
-Recovery must be bounded.
-
-Use limits such as:
-
-* maxAttemptsPerStep
-* maxRecoveryAttempts
-* maxLLMCallsPerExecution
-* maxToolCallsPerExecution
-* maxTotalCost
-
-Never allow an infinite retry or recovery loop.
-
-A successful recovery strategy may become procedural memory.
-
----
-
-# 11. Durable Execution
-
-Long-running workflows must not depend on an always-running process.
-
-Use Inngest.
-
-Expected lifecycle:
-
-execute
-→ checkpoint
-→ sleep/wait
-→ wake
-→ restore state
-→ continue
-
-Durable steps should contain external side effects.
-
-Be careful with operations whose previous result is unknown.
-
----
-
-# 12. Idempotency
-
-External side effects must be designed carefully.
-
-Use idempotency keys when appropriate.
-
-Pay particular attention to:
-
-* form submissions
-* resource creation
-* messages
-* bookings
-* mutations
-* purchases
-
-Never blindly retry a side effect when the previous request may have succeeded.
-
----
-
-# 13. Approval Boundary
-
-Consequential actions should follow:
-
-READ
-→ REASON
-→ ACTION PROPOSAL
-→ APPROVAL
-→ EXECUTE
-
-Do not allow the model to silently perform consequential actions.
-
-Read-only operations can generally execute without approval.
-
----
-
-# 14. Memory Architecture
-
-Aevryn owns its MemoryStore abstraction.
-
-Initial implementation:
-
-PostgreSQL + pgvector.
-
-Do not make Mem0, Supermemory, or another hosted memory service the source of truth.
-
-Memory categories:
-
-1. Working memory
-2. Episodic memory
-3. Semantic memory
-4. Procedural memory
-
-Procedural memory is particularly important for self-healing.
-
-Example:
-
-A website changes.
-
-The old extraction method fails.
-
-Aevryn discovers a new successful method.
-
-Aevryn stores that strategy.
-
-A future execution can retrieve and reuse it.
-
-Memory should use a deliberate policy.
-
-Do not store everything automatically.
-
-The LLM may propose memory candidates.
-
-The runtime decides whether to persist them.
-
-Memory must always respect user/workflow ownership.
-
-Never leak memory across users.
-
----
-
-# 15. Events
-
-Events describe things that happened.
-
-Examples:
-
-workflow.created
-workflow.started
-workflow.completed
-workflow.failed
-
-execution.started
-execution.completed
-execution.failed
-
-tool.called
-tool.completed
-tool.failed
-
-observation.created
-
-recovery.started
-recovery.completed
-recovery.failed
-
-workflow.sleeping
-workflow.resumed
-
-Events should be immutable.
-
-Do not use events as a replacement for current state.
-
----
-
-# 16. Database Rules
-
-Initial domain entities:
-
-* users
-* workflows
-* workflow_executions
-* workflow_steps
-* agent_states
-* observations
-* tool_executions
-* recovery_attempts
-* memories
-* events
-* schedules
-* notifications
-
-Do not create unnecessary tables.
-
-Indexes must correspond to actual query patterns.
-
-Use foreign keys.
-
-Use timestamptz for timestamps.
-
-Use UTC.
-
-Use optimistic concurrency where concurrent state updates are possible.
-
-Persisted schemas that may evolve should include schemaVersion where appropriate.
-
----
-
-# 17. IDs
-
-Use prefixed ULIDs for externally visible domain entities.
-
-Examples:
-
-wf_01K...
-exe_01K...
-step_01K...
-tool_01K...
-mem_01K...
-evt_01K...
-rec_01K...
-
-Do not use sequential public identifiers.
-
-Do not put sensitive information into IDs.
-
-Generate IDs with the `ids` utility from `@aevryn/db` (e.g. `ids.workflow()`,
-`ids.execution()`), implemented in `packages/db/src/ids.ts`. Validate with
-`isValidId(prefix, id)`.
-
-The same prefixes must stay in sync with the `ID_PREFIXES` map there.
-
----
-
-# 18. Naming Conventions
-
-## TypeScript
-
-Variables/functions:
-
-camelCase
-
-Classes/interfaces/types:
-
-PascalCase
-
-React components:
-
-PascalCase
-
-## JSON
-
-camelCase
-
-## PostgreSQL
-
-snake_case
-
-## Environment variables
-
-UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
-
-## HTTP routes
-
-/api/v1/<resource>
-
-Use kebab-case where route naming requires a multi-word resource.
-
-## Events
-
-dot.separated
-
-## Files
-
-Prefer kebab-case unless a framework convention requires otherwise.
-
----
-
-# 19. API Contract
-
-Use versioned APIs:
-
-/api/v1/...
-
-Successful response:
-
-{
-"data": {},
-"error": null,
-"meta": {
-"requestId": "req_..."
-}
-}
-
-Error response:
-
-{
-"data": null,
-"error": {
-"code": "ERROR_CODE",
-"message": "Human-readable message.",
-"details": null
-},
-"meta": {
-"requestId": "req_..."
-}
-}
-
-Every request should have a requestId.
-
-Propagate requestId into relevant workflow/execution/tool logs.
-
-Use appropriate HTTP status codes.
-
-Async workflow creation may return 202.
-
----
-
-# 20. Security
-
-Never store secrets in:
-
-* workflow state
-* memory
-* observations
-* tool inputs
-* tool outputs
-* events
-* logs
-
-Never log:
-
-* API keys
-* passwords
-* cookies
-* authorization headers
-* access tokens
-* secrets
-
-Redact sensitive values.
-
-Validate environment variables at startup.
-
-External inputs must be validated.
-
----
-
-# 21. Observability
-
-Use structured logs.
-
-Useful fields include:
-
-* requestId
-* workflowId
-* executionId
-* stepId
-* toolCallId
-* tool
-* provider
-* durationMs
-* errorCode
-
-Do not log entire prompts by default.
-
-Do not log secrets.
-
-Logs should allow a developer to reconstruct what happened during an execution without exposing sensitive data.
-
----
-
-# 22. Testing
-
-Use:
-
-* Vitest for unit/integration tests
-
-Prioritize testing:
-
-* state transitions
-* workflow lifecycle
-* capability validation
-* failure classification
-* retry behavior
-* recovery
-* memory isolation
-* idempotency
-* sleep/resume
-
-Prefer behavior-based tests.
-
-Do not test implementation details unnecessarily.
-
-Never delete or weaken a failing test just to make CI pass.
-
----
-
-# 23. Dependency Rules
-
-Before adding a dependency:
-
-1. Check whether the project already provides the functionality.
-2. Check whether an existing dependency can solve the problem.
-3. Determine whether the dependency is genuinely required.
-4. Prefer small, focused dependencies.
-5. Avoid duplicate libraries solving the same problem.
-
-Do not add:
-
-* Redis
-* Kafka
-* Temporal
-* another workflow engine
-* another vector database
-* LangChain
-* CrewAI
-
-unless a future requirement explicitly justifies it.
-
----
-
-# 24. Implementation Rules
-
-Do not implement the entire product in one pass.
-
-Work in vertical slices.
-
-Before making a major change:
-
-1. Inspect the repository.
-2. Read relevant architecture documentation.
-3. Identify existing abstractions.
-4. Plan the change.
-5. Implement the smallest correct change.
-6. Typecheck.
-7. Lint.
-8. Test.
-9. Verify runtime behavior.
-10. Review architecture.
-11. Commit.
-
-Never claim a feature works without actually verifying it.
-
-Never silently ignore compiler, test, lint, or runtime errors.
-
-Do not weaken types to bypass errors.
-
-Do not disable validation to make an integration work.
-
-Do not introduce infrastructure without a requirement.
-
----
-
-# 25. Initial Implementation Order
-
-Build in this order.
-
-## Phase 1 - Foundation
-
-* repository structure
-* agent runtime
-* capability abstraction
-* Anakin adapter
-* one working web capability
-* first vertical slice
-
-## Phase 2 - Persistence
-
-* workflows
-* executions
-* steps
-* state
-* database
-
-## Phase 3 - Durability
-
-* Inngest
-* durable steps
-* retries
-* checkpointing
-
-## Phase 4 - Decision Runtime
-
-* structured decisions
-* state patches
-* lifecycle transitions
-
-## Phase 5 - Recovery
-
-* failure classification
-* recovery attempts
-* bounded recovery
-* validation
-
-## Phase 6 - Memory
-
-* MemoryStore
-* PostgreSQL memory
-* pgvector
-* semantic retrieval
-* procedural memory
-
-## Phase 7 - Long-running Workflows
-
-* sleep
-* wake
-* schedules
-* webhooks
-* asynchronous provider operations
-
-## Phase 8 - Browser Recovery
-
-* Anakin Browser API
-* Stagehand
-* structural recovery
-
-## Phase 9 - Product UI
-
-* objective creation
-* workflow status
-* execution timeline
-* observations
-* recovery visibility
-* memory visibility where useful
-
-## Phase 10 - Hardening
-
-* testing
-* security
-* observability
-* error handling
-* demo reliability
-
-Do not skip ahead because a later feature looks more interesting.
-
----
-
-# 26. First Vertical Slice
-
-The first working feature is intentionally small.
-
-Example:
-
-User:
-
-"Find the latest information about React."
-
-Flow:
-
-Next.js UI
-→ API
-→ AgentTask/runtime
-→ AI SDK agent
-→ searchWeb capability
-→ Anakin Search
-→ structured result
-→ response
-
-Do not implement memory, recovery, browser automation, or long-running scheduling before this works.
-
----
-
-# 27. Git Commit Convention
-
-Every commit must use this format:
-
-<type>(<major-area>): <detailed description>
-
-The scope must contain ONE major word describing the primary area changed.
-
-Examples:
-
-feat(agent): implement structured capability execution and validated tool results
-
-feat(workflow): add durable workflow execution with persisted lifecycle state
-
-feat(memory): add PostgreSQL memory storage with semantic retrieval foundations
-
-fix(recovery): prevent repeated structural recovery attempts after exhaustion
-
-refactor(state): separate workflow state updates from execution history persistence
-
-test(runtime): cover capability failures and bounded execution transitions
-
-docs(architecture): document durable execution and provider boundary decisions
-
-chore(tooling): configure repository validation and development scripts
-
-The description should be detailed enough to explain WHAT changed and, when useful, WHY.
-
-Avoid meaningless commits such as:
-
-bad:
-feat(agent): stuff
-
-bad:
-fix: things
-
-bad:
-update: changes
-
-bad:
-wip
-
-bad:
-misc
-
-The scope must be one major word.
-
-Examples of valid scopes:
-
-agent
-workflow
-state
-memory
-recovery
-database
-api
-ui
-anakin
-inngest
-testing
-tooling
-docs
-security
-
-Do not use multiple scopes:
-
-bad:
-feat(agent/workflow): ...
-
-bad:
-feat(agent,workflow): ...
-
-Use the dominant area instead.
-
-Before committing, ensure the commit contains one coherent logical change.
-
-Do not combine unrelated features into one commit.
-
----
-
-# 28. Commit Verification
-
-Before every commit:
-
-1. Review changed files.
-2. Check for accidental files.
-3. Check for secrets.
-4. Run relevant tests.
-5. Run typecheck.
-6. Run lint/format checks.
-7. Confirm the change is logically coherent.
-8. Write a detailed commit message following the required format.
-
-Never commit secrets or .env files containing real credentials.
-
----
-
-# 29. Architecture Integrity
-
-If a requested feature conflicts with the architecture:
-
-Do not silently redesign the system.
-
-Explain:
-
-1. What conflicts.
-2. Why it conflicts.
-3. What alternatives exist.
-4. Which alternative you recommend.
-
-Only then make a major architectural change.
-
-The goal is not maximum abstraction.
-
-The goal is a simple, durable, understandable architecture that can evolve.
-
----
-
-# 30. OpenCode Behavior
-
-When working on Aevryn:
-
-* Read AGENTS.md first.
-* Inspect before editing.
-* Do not assume files exist.
-* Do not invent APIs without checking installed packages.
-* Do not invent provider behavior.
-* Prefer official documentation when implementing integrations.
-* Keep changes incremental.
-* Verify changes.
-* Report what was actually verified.
-* Stop at the requested milestone.
-
-Never implement future milestones simply because they are described in the roadmap.
-
-The current milestone is authoritative.
-
----
-
-# 31. Definition of Done
-
-A feature is not complete merely because code exists.
-
-A feature is complete when:
-
-* implementation exists
-* types are correct
-* validation exists where required
-* tests cover important behavior
-* lint passes
-* typecheck passes
-* runtime behavior has been verified
-* architecture boundaries remain intact
-* secrets are not exposed
-* documentation is updated when the architecture changed
-* a coherent commit can describe the change

# ENV — Variables & User-Suppliable Keys

Three layers: **server/infra env** (Vercel/Next server, never client),
**user workspace keys** (entered by user in Workflow Settings → Agent/Env tab,
stored in DB, encrypted), and **per-thread overrides** (rare, optional).

## Existing env (old backend → what to keep)

| Var | Used by (old) | New use |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` / `DIRECT_URL` | drizzle pg | → Supabase project connection string (keep, used by drizzle) |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` / `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | better-auth | **DELETE** (Supabase Auth owns sessions) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | unused today | keep — supabase-js client |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | unused today | keep — anon role for RLS/DATA API |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | — | **ADD** server-only, storage uploads + admin (never NEXT_PUBLIC) |
| `ANAKIN_API_KEY` / `ANAKIN_BASE_URL` | agent adapters | fallback default; user can override per workspace |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` / `GROQ_MODEL` | runtime | fallback defaults; per workspace override |
| `MEM0_API_KEY` | workflow mem0 | fallback; per workspace override |
| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` / `SIGNING_KEY` / `APP_ID` | inngest client | keep |
| `WEBHOOK_BASE_URL` | webhook-board | keep |
| `AGENT_MAX_STEPS` / `AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS` / `RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | inngest | keep as server caps (hard ceiling) |

## NEW env (definitive list, final)

```
# --- Supabase ---
DATABASE_URL                # postgres connection for drizzle (direct)
DIRECT_URL                  # pooler direct url (non-pooled, for migrations)
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL    # client
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY  # client anon (never secret)
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY   # server only — storage bucket mgmt, user creation
SUPABASE_AUTH_SECRET        # optional: for verifying webhook JWT from auth hooks

# --- Inngest ---
INNGEST_EVENT_KEY
INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY
INNGEST_APP_ID

# --- Webhook interop ---
WEBHOOK_BASE_URL            # base url for generated /api/v1/hooks/:token urls

# --- Defaults (single fallback key each; user overrides per-workspace in UI) ---
ANAKIN_API_KEY
ANAKIN_BASE_URL             # default https://api.anakin.io/v1
GROQ_API_KEY
GROQ_MODEL                  # default text model, e.g. openai/gpt-oss-20b
MEM0_API_KEY

# --- Server hard caps (clamp user values; not editable by user) ---
AGENT_MAX_STEPS             # default 5      — ceiling
AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS        # default 50     — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS       # default 900    — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD      # default 1      — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS # default 604800 — ceiling
RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS       # default 2      — ceiling

# --- Model routing (per category; fall back from workspace → env default) ---
TEXT_MODEL                   # alias of GROQ_MODEL default (kept by name parity)
IMAGE_MODEL                  # default e.g. groq/text2img or provider, optional
SPEECH_MODEL                 # optional
TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL          # optional
VIDEO_MODEL                  # optional (future)
```

> Client (`packages/env/src/web.ts`) must expose only:
> `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
> Everything else stays server-only. `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION` respected.

## Where the USER enters their own keys (UI)

Primary → **Workflow Settings dialog → "Agent" tab** (rename of
"Instructions"), with an **"Environment"** subsection:

- Groq API key + Groq model (text)
- Anakin API key + base URL
- Mem0 API key
- (secondary) Image / Speech / Transcription / Video model overrides

Stored in DB table `workspace_api_keys`:
`workspace_id | user_id | provider | key_name | key_value(encrypted) | created_at`.

Resolution order at call time:
```
1. member of a SHARED workspace + user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
     → member's OWN Personal workspace keys
2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
3. env default
```
`workflow_api_keys` optional per-thread override keyed same way (rare).
Encryption: AES-256-GCM with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env (add to server env) — or
Supabase Vault (`vault.create_secret`) if service_role available. Recommend
**Supabase Vault** — no extra env key, native audit.

> Note: ChatComposer token slider = "max tokens per chat request" — maps to
> `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, NOT a run budget. Server caps
> (`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` etc.) remain hard ceilings.

## Best placement reasoning
- Workspace is the right scope: keys belong to a workspace, reusable in the
  `PERSONAL` workspace and future ones. Thread-level is pointless UX (user
  shouldn't re-enter per thread); we allow per-thread override but never require.
- Server retains hard caps so a user cannot self-grant unlimited budgets.
- Never ship keys to client — tools run server-side (Inngest/route), so only
  server reads them.

- Queue durability (sequential) + auto-approve + notifications chip +
  per-workspace keys + media (image/transcription).
- No hardcoded mock data; all mocked UI wired to DB; tRPC removed.

# ARCHITECTURE — Full New Backend + Frontend Logic

Replaces the old tRPC + regex-decision + god-class backend. The system becomes:

```
Browser (Next.js client, zustand stores)
   │  useChat (Vercel AI SDK @ai-sdk/react 4.x)
   ▼
/workspace/[threadId]   (client page, no full reload on threadId swap)
   │
   ▼  POST /api/chat (ChatTransport → streamText)
   │
   ├── live (fast) tools: askUserQuestion, showPlan, editPlan, memory tools,
   │                      HTTP request tool, media tools (image/transcription live)
   │
   └── durable (Anakin/Inngest) tools: delegateAgenticWork (one tool)
               │
               ▼  inngest.send("thread/run")
               ▼  Inngest fn "thread-runner" streams run_activities rows
               ▼  Supabase Realtime → ChatMessage updates live in place
```

## A. Auth (Supabase, Google only, MVP)

- Root `page.tsx` = login screen. `supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider:"google"})`.
- `onLinkIdentity`/redirect to `/workspace` after signup.
- Post-signup flow: pre-questions driven by a JSON config (role/usecase/goal,
  multi+single select; user edits the JSON, app maps it to QuestionFlow). Answers
  → `user_profiles.pre_answers`. If signup exists but profile row missing → auto
  navigate to onboarding (create on demand).
- `useSupabaseUser()` hook (zustand + Supabase client). Middleware/proxy
  (`src/proxy.ts` evlog) still runs; tRPC session shim removed — server routes
  read `createServerClient` session from cookies.
- Sessions: Supabase handles refresh (`@supabase/ssr` cookie-based). Server
  side: `createServerClient` with anon/publishable; protected route checks user.

## B. Realtime plumbing

- **Supabase Realtime** on tables: `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
  `approval_requests`, `notifications` (private channels, JWT-auth user filters).
- Client hooks: `useChatRealtime(threadId)` merges live broadcast rows into the
  chat store / useChat message list. **This is how Inngest-produced activity
  reaches the UI** (durable work streams to an open chat).
- Room id convention `thread:{threadId}` on Realtime channel.

## C. Chat transport & message appending (the "no new message every tool" rule)

Streaming in web via `POST /api/chat` using `ChatTransport` protocol:
- Drive `messages` from DB via `chat_messages`, feed to `streamText`.
- **Live LLM path**: `streamText({model, messages, tools, toolApproval,
  stopWhen: isStepCount(maxSteps), system: composeSystem(workflow, plan, memory)})`
  → `toUIMessageStream` → `createUIMessageStreamResponse`. Returns typed
  `UIMessage` parts; `useChat`/`Chat` client keeps ONE assistant message alive
  and appends tool parts to it.
- **Durable path**: when a tool needs Inngest (Anakin, browser, sleep/schedule),
  the route/handler calls `inngest.send("thread/run", …)` and returns a
  "delegated" tool part with the `run_id`; UI shows ThinkingSteps derived from
  `run_activities` streamed in. When the run completes, the ChatMessage gets a
  final assistant part (result text). No new message bubbles for sub-steps —
  everything appends to the same assistant message.
- **New ChatMessage(assistant) triggers** ONLY: error, warning, workflow stops
  unexpectedly, user stops → user clicks Run again. (Per user rule.)

```tsx
// client pseudocode — the appending contract
const { messages, sendMessage, addToolResult, stop } = useChat({ api: "/api/chat", id: threadId });
// useChat actually uses Chat/DefaultChatTransport — bridge in provider
```

## D. Tool surface (LLM-invocable, zod schemas, NEVER hardcoded)

| Tool | When | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `askQuestion` | clarifying questions (any time LLM needs) | live — returns `AskUserQuestion[]` JSON → UI renders ask-user-questions (MCQ) |
| `showPlan` | ONLY when user explicitly asks to plan/workflow (NO auto-plan) | live — returns `{steps: [...], header}` → AccordionGroup |
| `editPlan` | add/remove/update any step | live — persists `plan_steps` |
| `finalizeAndInject` | user approves → bind thread↔workflow, set status | live + sends thread/run if "run" chosen |
| `bindWorkflow` (variant) | approve-but-not-run | live — bind only, workflow idle; Run button appears, Stop hidden. Run toggles→Stop while running |
| `storeMemory` / `searchMemory` | thread + global memory (mem0) | live (mem0 low-latency); ONE mem0 store per user, thread scoped by metadata |
| `httpRequest` | user bearer token, arbitrary HTTP | live — raw fetch; https-only, private-IP blocked, size/max-redirect caps |
| `delegateAgenticWork` | ANY Anakin capability (search/scrape/crawl/map/research/wire/browser + schedule) | durable → Inngest `thread/run`; returns run_id |
| `generateImage` / `transcribeAudio` | media generation requests | live when `IMAGE_MODEL`/`TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` set per workspace/env |

- `askQuestion` → `AskUserQuestion` schema (packages/ui
  `ask-user-questions.tsx:37`) — single zod schema shared server+client.
- Auto-approve switch: toolApproval config + `approval_requests` row status
  auto-"approved" when workflow.auto_approve; system message emitted
  "auto-approved via settings".
- **NO auto-plan/wiring**: LLM answers plain text, never auto-creates a plan or
  binds a workflow on its own. `showPlan` only fires after user explicitly asks
  ("create a workflow / plan this"). A 2nd user message is NOT a plan trigger.
- **Attachments → LLM-readable**: image/pdf/video dropped into ChatComposer get
  converted to LLM input parts (image → data URL / base64 image part; pdf →
  extracted text part) before the call; media tools return real content.

## E. Durable execution (Inngest): `thread/run`

- ONE event: `thread/run` (down from pile). `thread-runner` function:
  1. fetch everything from DB (thread, plan, memory summaries, previous runs).
  2. `generateText`/`ToolLoopAgent` with the SAME tool set minus the durable
     re-delegation (no recursion);
  3. persist each step/tool into `runs` + `run_activities` + broadcast.
  4. sleep/resume via `runs.status=sleeping` + schedule-tick (FIXED: add proper
     Inngest `triggers: [{ event:... }]` or `cron`) — and register ALL functions
     in `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts` serve list.
  5. notify on completion/failure → `notifications`.
- Idempotency: `runs.status` gate `pending→running` with `select … for update`
  in Postgres; retries honor existing activity instead of re-running.
- Cost caps: check BEFORE each step (realtime), not after the run (fix the
  old post-hoc bug).

## F. Frontend state (zustand)

- Zustand stores (each `[thread]`, `[sidebar]`, `[chatComposer]`, `[ui/theme]`,
  `[auth]`) — keeps server components pure; zustand used max; no useState sprawl.
- `threadId` navigation: Next.js `router.push('/workspace/'+id, { scroll:false })`
  updating only param; page reads `params.threadId` once → store. ChatComposer
  layout: centered when no messages → bottom once first message exists.
- ChatComposer: queue (ordered, editable, removable, durable-backend),
  token-quality slider formula: `maxTokens per CHAT request` (this is what the
  slider means; maps to `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, not a run budget),
  file/image/pdf attach → compress (canvas, WebP, quality 0.8, max 2000px) →
  Supabase Storage → `files` row + `UIMessage` attachments.
- Queue `chat_messages.status=queued`: on run finish, drain SEQUENTIALLY —
  deliver message, wait for that response to finish, then next (no parallel
  queue burst). Edited/reordered queue → DB rows updated in place, order kept.

## G. Memory (mem0, ONE place per user, thread-scoped)

- ONE mem0 store per app user (as chosen): every thread's memories live there,
  scoped by `metadata.threadId`. `storeMemory`/`searchMemory` tools:
  - thread scope: `{scope:"thread", threadId}` — memories only reprompted for
    that thread.
  - global scope: `{scope:"global"}` — **program-given memory injected
    beforehand**, works across ALL workspaces/threads/apps for that user (not
    per-workspace). E.g. capability schemas, user prefs, standing instructions.
- `packages/agent/src/adapters/README.md:1` resolution: adapter schemas exposed
  to LLM via GLOBAL memory (per decision) — one tool `listCapabilities` returns
  schemas; keeps them OO-reflectable.

## I. Permission model — invites, roles, sharing (locked answers)

### Role set (ONE model everywhere)
`owner | editor | viewer` — **no admin**. | Action | owner | editor | viewer | thread-guest |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| rename / delete workspace, keys, settings | ✅ | — | — | — |
| manage members (invite/role/remove) | ✅ | — | — | — |
| create / rename / delete groups & threads | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| edit plans, bind workflows | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| send msgs, run/stop, approve approvals | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ |
| view history / runs / plan | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| rename / rebind / re-share / delete shared thread | ✅ | — | — | — |
> thread-guest = the person invited to a SPECIFIC thread (thread share). Editor
> = member of the shared workspace.

### Workspace invite (join the REAL workspace)
1. Owner (only) copies workspace invite link / shares by email → `invites` row
   (`kind=workspace`, role editor|viewer chosen at invite).
2. Invitee accepts → `workspace_members` row (role as invited). NO copy, no new
   workspace — it's the owner's actual workspace. Workspace appears in the
   invitee's top-left switcher (badge on the button) → switching in shows ALL
   groups + threads (all members see everything).
3. Members chat/run using the **workspace's keys** (owner pays) UNLESS profile
   toggle "use my own keys in invited workspaces" is on → member's own
   workspace keys are used. `get_workspace_key` RPC + key-service honor this.
4. Owner can change roles / remove / revoke anytime. Editor can delete any
   thread/group (even others'). Viewer read-only.

### Thread share (guest in YOUR sidebar)
1. Owner toggles `threads.share_enabled` and copies the thread share link
   (per-thread; the "list of my threads + switch" UI in Members/Share).
2. Invitee accepts → `thread_shares` row. The LIVE SAME thread (not a copy)
   appears in the invitee's OWN workspace sidebar under the **INVITES system
   group** (created locked+empty at signup; only fills via accepted invites),
   with a Badge on the thread button and on the header. Both users
   chat in the same realtime thread.
3. Invitee's messages use **their own keys**; their name shows on user bubbles.
4. Owner revokes by flipping share_enabled / deleting the share.

### Keys resolution order (chat / run)
```
1. member in a shared workspace + prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
      → member's OWN Personal workspace keys (type: groq|anakin|mem0|…)
2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
3. env defaults (ANAKIN_API_KEY / GROQ_API_KEY / MEM0_API_KEY / models)
```

## K. Flow verification scenarios (must "just work")

1. **"Hi"** → user text only, LLM plain text, NO tool call, NO new workflow.
2. **"plan me a laptop comparison"** → LLM askQuestion (MCQ) → user answers →
   showPlan accordion → workflowApproval (approve/decline/bind/run) → bind →
   `thread/run` → ThinkingSteps stream research/scrape sub-tasks into the SAME
   assistant message → final answer text appended.
3. **"scrape X.com profile" (no plan)** → delegateAgenticWork → durable run →
   run_activities stream → final text in same message.
4. **user closes tab mid-run** → run continues in Inngest; reopening
   workspace reloads `chat_messages` + `run_activities` → renders state.
5. **queued "delete workflow" while run active** → message queued durable;
   once run completes → queued delivered SEQUENTIALLY (wait each).
6. **auto-approve ON** → approval resolves instantly + system message.
7. **workspace invite** → invitee opens link, accepts → workspace in switcher
   (badge), ALL threads visible, chats charge workspace keys (owner) unless
   invitee's "use my own keys" toggle → own keys.
8. **thread share** → owner toggles share, guest accepts → SAME live thread in
   guest's INVITES group + header badge, guest chats with OWN keys + name on
   bubbles, cannot edit plan/rename; owner revoke removes access instantly.
9. **deleted thread** → soft-archive 30 days (trash), recover → live;
   after 30 days hard-delete (incl. runs/activities/files).
10. **"re-run last run"** → play a rerun (trigger=rerun) with same plan, no
    new chat; hits new `runs` row, streams activities again.
11. **first message** → auto-titles thread; title editable after.

## L. Non-goals / pinned decisions
- Markdown rendering: FUTURE (write API to be parser-friendly — parts, no
  prose-heavy gating). Output contract ready for it.
- Media generation: IMAGE + TRANSCRIPTION SHIPPED in MVP (lazy-load provider
  when `IMAGE_MODEL`/`TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` configured); SPEECH/VIDEO stay schemas
  only until models exist. Attachments always converted to LLM-readable parts.
- Sub-agents in parallel: FUTURE phase (see FEATURES.md); design tool outputs as
  containers so sub-agent results merge into `run_activities`.
- Creating MULTIPLE owned workspaces: FUTURE (pro tier). MVP = 1 owned
  Personal + unlimited JOINED workspaces (via invite).
- Shared-thread plan editing by guests: OFF (owner/editor only).

## Product features (locked in docs; see NOTES "Decisions" & PLAN.md)
1. **Soft-archive delete**: deleting a thread/workflow sets `threads.deleted_at`;
   recoverable 30 days (trash), then hard-delete incl. Storage. Never silent.
2. **Smart auto-title**: thread title automatically set from the first user
   message (truncated); rename still available. No blank "New thread".
3. **One Run mental model**: Run button AND the LLM both fire `thread/run`
   (same event). WorkflowApproval dialog = max 4 buttons: Approve+Run /
   Approve / Decline / Edit plan. No dead dropdowns.
4. **Model presets**: Agent/Env tab shows a per-provider list of known model
   ids (searchable) + free-text override; picks write `workspace_api_keys.model_name`.
5. **Share preview page**: share link lands on a preview (thread title + owner
   name only, NO content) with Accept — content stays private until accepted.
6. **Export/import thread**: single JSON (plan + steps + key messages,
   keys stripped) for export/import — template/reuse path.
7. **Re-run**: from a past Run play a rerun with the same plan, no new chat
   (`runs.rerun_of`, trigger=rerun).

# DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)

Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).

## Conventions
- Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
  prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
  `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
  now()`, `updated_at`.
- All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
  or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
- RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
  (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
- text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.

api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
```

## Supabase specifics
- Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
- **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
  `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
- **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
  dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
  CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
- **RLS policy list**:
  - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
    files (+ own invites).
  - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
    chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
    OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
  - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
    `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
    group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
  - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
    `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
    workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
    exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
    → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
- **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
  `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
  `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
  (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.

## Why this shape (reasoning)
- `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
  sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
- `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
  custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
  until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
  ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
- `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
  accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
- `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
  run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
  `threads.user_id`).
- `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
  replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
- `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
  directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
  killing the god-table smell.
- `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
  by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
- Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
  → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

# PROMPTS — Single Prompt Library

ONE file, everything exported, imported elsewhere. No string prompts inline.
Located at `packages/agent/src/prompts.ts` (replaces `runtime.ts` inline consts
and planning inline text). Split by role.

```
packages/agent/src/prompts.ts
  system/       — immutable / global behavior
  agent/        — chat agent persona + tool policy
  planning/     — planning-mode instructions
  durable/      — thread-runner instructions (Inngest)
  memory/       — memory tool guidance
  http/         — http tool policy
  subagents/    — (future) container-agent instructions
```

## 1. `SYSTEM_PERSONA`
Intro to aevryn: name, tone (concise, agentic), bounds (chat-only; never
pretend to act outside tools), markdown allowed.

## 2. `SYSTEM_TOOL_POLICY` (replaces TOOL_SELECTION_INSTRUCTIONS)
- Never call a tool for greetings/hi/basic Q&A — plain text.
- **NO auto-planning**: never call `showPlan`/`bindWorkflow`/`finalizeAndInject`
  unless the user EXPLICITLY asks you to make a plan / create a workflow. The
  second message is NOT a plan trigger. Plain chat until the user asks.
- Every Anakin / browser action goes through `delegateAgenticWork` (durable),
  never directly in chat.
- askQuestion used for ANY uncertainty the answer changes cost of next step.
- showPlan AFTER questions; workflowApproval via `finalizeAndInject` only after
  plan accepted.
- plan editability: LLM may call editPlan at any time post-plan.
- Respect auto-approve: if enabled, resolve approval automatically and say
  "auto-approved via settings" as system message.
- Media: `generateImage`/`transcribeAudio` available only when their model is
  configured for this workspace.

## 3. `PLANNING_SYSTEM` (works with showPlan/askQuestion flow)
"Given the objective, plan scope: ask clarifying questions first when needed.
When you're ready, build the plan. Each step must be actionable and
factored < 20 lines of description. Order critical steps first."
Output: structured via `showPlan(plan)` tool `{steps:[{title,description}]}`.

## 4. `PLAN_WORKFLOW_APPROVAL` (binding message)
"You presented the final plan. Waiting for workflow binding approval
(approve / decline / bind / approve-and-run). Do NOT begin actions before
approval. If declined, discard plan and ask what changed."

## 5. `DURABLE_RUNNER_SYSTEM` (thread-runner in Inngest)
"You are executing plan step N/total. Only the tools you have may run.
Edit plan only via editPlan. Errors: classify and retry with guidance, don't
silently stop."

## 6. `MEMORY_TOOL_GUIDE`
"storeMemory: natural-language facts user wants remembered, category semantic.
searchMemory: retrieve with query matching intent, scope thread|global."
SCOPES (locked): thread → metadata.threadId of the CURRENT chat; global →
program-given facts injected beforehand, available everywhere (all workspaces).

## 7. `HTTP_TOOL_POLICY`
"httpRequest: ONLY for user-requested integration. Send bearer from the user
token field. Do not follow redirects to unexpected hosts. Timeout & size caps."

## 8. `SUB_AGENT_CONTAINER` (future)
"Result JSON: merged into run_activities with type=container. Return markdown
ar interesting findings."

## Usage contract
- `buildSystem(workflow, plan, memorySummary)` composes 1..N prompts with glue.
- Provider-level vs user-level: nothing user-facing; keys/model come from
  workspace_api_keys via key-service BEFORE streamText.
- Single source of truth: importing pkg `prompts` anywhere = consistent.

## Out-of-scope prompts
- Retry guidance / recovery hints: move to `prompts.ts` DURABLE section (was
  inlined in execution-run.ts): keep same codes (RECOVERY_HINTS) but centralized.

# Aevryn — Code Review Observations

Audited: monorepo at `D:\github-desktop\aevryn` (read-only).
Scope: whole repo described in `AGENTS.md`, `internal/` decisions/plans, all
`NEWTODO` markers, and the live data paths they depend on.

---

## 1. What the system is today

A persistent web-agent platform. The legacy flow:

```
Next.js UI (hardcoded demo)
→ tRPC router  packages/api/src/routers/agent.ts  (630 lines)
→ WorkflowService  packages/workflow/src/services/workflow-service.ts  (1517 lines)
→ 13 repositories → Drizzle → PostgreSQL
   +  Inngest functions:
       execution-run.ts (914 lines)   — the whole agent loop
       schedule-tick.ts  (143 lines)  — cron + sleep/wake
       notification-notifier.ts       — webhook delivery
```

Capabilities (`packages/agent`): 13 registered capabilities wrapping 6 Anakin
adapters (search/scrape/crawl/map/research/wire) + browser sessions + memory +
schedules. Approval-gated: `wireAction`, `browserSessionCreate/Rename/Delete`.

LLM (Groq via Vercel AI SDK `ai` v7): `runAgent` in
`packages/agent/src/runtime.ts` drives a single `generateText` loop with
`isStepCount(maxSteps)` and the SDK's `toolApproval` gate. Plans and runtime
decisions are extracted from the model's final text with `/\`\`\`json...\`\`\`/`
regex in `packages/inngest/src/functions/execution-run.ts:48`.

Re-architecture already decided in `internal/plans/2026-09-10-aevryn-rearchitecture/`
and `internal/ALL-DECISIONS.md`:
thread === workflow, first message ≠ objective, planning output =
`AskUserQuestion[]` (MCQ), chat streams in the web app via `POST /api/chat`
(`useChat` + zod tools `askUserQuestion` / `showPlan` / `finalizeAndInject`),
ONE Inngest `execution/run` event only on plan approval, Supabase Auth,
mem0 per-thread memory. `apps/web/src/app/workspace/[threadId]/page.tsx` is the
empty stub that must become this.

---

## 2. NEWTODO inventory (the user's own work order)

| # | File:line | Ask |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `packages/auth/README.md:1` | Rebuild auth — Supabase Google signup ONLY |
| 2 | `packages/api/README.md:1` | Rebuild API ("only when 100% sure") |
| 3 | `packages/agent/src/README.md:1` | Fix `runtime.ts` hardcoded prompts → real prompt library module |
| 4 | `packages/agent/src/adapters/README.md:1,3` | Decide how adapter schemas reach the LLM (tool call vs global memory); note: schemas already live in capabilities via `inputSchema` |
| 5 | `packages/agent/src/adapters/scrape.ts:1` | Verify exact `@anakin-io/sdk` `ScrapeFormat` list (current union may be wrong) |
| 6 | `packages/workflow/README.md:1` | Rebuild `workflow` package after new plan |
